hypothesis: A train/inference-consistent shared null-action path will reproduce the action-conditioned future-H3 signal in both seeds when true, null and shuffled actions are evaluated through the same fitted model.
single_variable: Relative to raw-target C35, C37 changes only the action-control route: the conditioned model receives 10% structured whole-sample zero-action dropout during training and is gated by paired true-versus-null inference from that same model; data, features, architecture, optimizer, steps, seeds and shuffle gate remain fixed.
parent_baseline: C35 and C36 both retained strict FAIL because separately fitted independent models crossed the 1% gate in only one temporal seed each. A post-hoc diagnostic, not used as evidence, found that each frozen C35 conditioned model itself improved true versus zero action by 16.8%-22.6%; C37 preregisters a clean replication before making any mechanism claim.

decision.rationale: Both prior sweeps show repeated shuffle sensitivity while the separately trained independent arm changes ordering across seeds. MiniWorld's official shared null-conditioning path directly addresses that confound, and the strong post-hoc paired diagnostic justifies a clean preregistered replication rather than a retroactive gate change.
